# Results — Study 888 (CLO AAA Carry)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The claim under test: a **AAA-rated
CLO tranche** (JAAA since 2020-10, ICLO since 2022-12) pays a *real, mechanical, risk-adjusted*
pickup over cash and over same-rated IG corporates for structural complexity, while sitting
senior in the capital stack (~nil realized default). Offline & deterministic once cached; run
`python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number, as-of 2026-06-30 (the last complete
calendar month; the partial current month is dropped). Fingerprint `3568185876b2` (prices).*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily **total-return** closes (`auto_adjust=True`), **JAAA / ICLO / LQD / IEF / BKLN / BIL**, 2020-01-02 → 2026-06-30, **1,631** dated rows |
| Legs | **JAAA**, **ICLO** = AAA CLO ETFs (floating, senior tranche); **LQD** = IG corporates (~8y dur); **IEF** = 7-10y Treasuries; **BKLN** = un-tranched leveraged loans; **BIL** = 1-3m T-bills (the cash leg) |
| Signal | each leg's daily total return **minus BIL** (excess-of-cash); the AAA-CLO carry is that excess spread |
| Statistics | annualised excess mean/vol, the excess **Sharpe** with a **circular-block-bootstrap** 95% CI, a Newey-West (HAC, 10-lag) *t* on the daily excess, max drawdown; a ZIRP-vs-high-rate era cut; costed harvest + long/short trade; a 12-seed synthetic control |
| Execution / costs | ETF total-return NAV is already net of the ~0.20%/yr expense ratio; the costed harvest charges the ETF bid-ask (3 bps one-way × turnover); the isolation trade pays borrow + spread on both legs |

**Short history — named on the Signal axis.** JAAA has ~5.7y of tape, ICLO ~3.5y; the sample
spans one rate cycle (ZIRP → the 2022 hikes → a 5% plateau) but **no CLO credit-stress event**
— the March-2020 AAA-CLO mark-down predates JAAA. Every realized Sharpe below is an **upper
bound** on the true risk-adjusted edge.

## The headline — excess-of-cash (minus BIL) Sharpe race

Full available history per leg (annualised excess, vol, Sharpe [95% block-bootstrap CI],
HAC *t* on the daily excess, max drawdown), sorted by Sharpe:

| leg | window | n | excess %/yr | vol % | Sharpe | 95% CI | HAC *t* | maxDD % |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|:--:|--:|--:|
| **ICLO** | 2022-12 → 2026-06 | 889 | **+2.14** | 2.43 | **+0.88** | [+0.22, +2.31] | **+3.08** | −3.46 |
| **JAAA** | 2020-10 → 2026-06 | 1429 | **+1.38** | 1.63 | **+0.84** | [+0.09, +1.72] | **+2.33** | −2.60 |
| BKLN | 2020-01 → 2026-06 | 1630 | +1.82 | 7.71 | +0.24 | [−0.67, +1.14] | +0.53 | −24.17 |
| LQD | 2020-01 → 2026-06 | 1630 | −1.09 | 10.27 | −0.11 | [−0.85, +0.68] | −0.27 | −24.95 |
| IEF | 2020-01 → 2026-06 | 1630 | −2.42 | 7.46 | −0.33 | [−1.04, +0.37] | −0.90 | −23.92 |

The two AAA-CLO funds sit at the **top** of the excess-Sharpe race with **tiny** vol
(1.6-2.4%) and shallow drawdowns (≤3.5%). JAAA's carry is **+1.38%/yr** over cash for a
**Sharpe of +0.84** (HAC *t* = +2.33; the bootstrap CI keeps clear of zero, [+0.09, +1.72],
with only 1.5% of resamples negative). **ICLO independently confirms** (+0.88, *t* = +3.08). The
duration/credit alternatives (LQD, IEF) have **negative** excess Sharpe over a window that
contained the 2022 bond crash; the un-tranched loan collateral (BKLN) earns a comparable *raw*
excess but at ~5× the volatility and a −24% drawdown.

## The tell — the AAA tranche beats the loans it is carved from

The sharpest control is not corporate bonds but **BKLN** — the same leveraged loans held
un-tranched and below IG. JAAA (Sharpe **+0.84**, maxDD **−2.60%**) delivers a far better
*risk-adjusted* return than BKLN (Sharpe **+0.24**, maxDD **−24.17%**): the seniority /
tranching is doing real work, not merely repackaging loan beta.

## Head-to-head — JAAA excess minus each benchmark excess (== JAAA − bench)

| pair | window | n | diff %/yr | HAC *t* |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|
| JAAA − LQD | 2020-10 → 2026-06 | 1429 | **+4.10** | +1.23 |
| JAAA − IEF | 2020-10 → 2026-06 | 1429 | **+5.85** | +2.00 |
| JAAA − BKLN | 2020-10 → 2026-06 | 1429 | −0.86 | −0.60 |

JAAA handily out-carries duration (LQD, IEF) per dollar; against BKLN it is ~flat in *raw*
return — but earns it at a fraction of the risk (the risk-adjusted race above).

## Era cut — the carry is regime-dependent

| era | window | n | JAAA excess %/yr | Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| ZIRP (rates ~0) | 2020-10 → 2022-06 | 427 | **+0.00** | +0.00 | +0.00 |
| high-rate plateau | 2023-01 → 2026-06 | 875 | **+1.84** | +1.37 | +2.96 |

Essentially **all** the carry is the high-rate era: an excess-of-cash spread is proportionally
tiny when the base rate is zero, and AAA-CLO spreads widened through 2022H1, so the ZIRP window
is **flat** (not negative). A genuine but regime-bound edge.

## Tradability — a costed net edge survives, but the tail does not

(a) Buy-and-hold JAAA funded by cash; the ~0.20%/yr ER is already inside the NAV, so the extra
friction is only the ETF bid-ask (3 bps one-way × turnover):

| rebalances/yr | gross %/yr | charge % | net %/yr | Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 1 (buy-and-hold) | +1.38 | 0.03 | **+1.35** | +0.83 | +2.28 |
| 12 (needless churn) | +1.38 | 0.36 | **+1.02** | +0.62 | +1.72 |

(b) The relative isolation trade (long JAAA / short LQD, borrow 40 bps/yr + spread both legs):
gross +4.10%/yr − 1.12% charge → **net +2.98%/yr** (Sharpe +0.35, HAC *t* +0.89) — but it is
also short ~8y duration, a rate bet, not pure carry.

Costs are **not** the binding constraint: the harvest survives them easily and JAAA is a
>$20bn, tightly-traded fund (ample capacity). What makes it **Fragile** rather than
**Investable**: the whole ~1.4%/yr *is* the compensation for a tail (illiquidity / senior-CLO
mark-down) that the calm ~5.7y sample never charged — the realized −2.6% drawdown wildly
understates a crisis (AAA CLOs fell ~5-10% intraday in March 2020, before JAAA existed). A
single such event erases years of carry, so the realized Sharpe flatters the true edge.

## Synthetic positive control — the machinery is unbiased

Deterministic seeded daily world with a planted excess-of-cash carry (+1.2%/yr) plus a high-vol
"duration" decoy; the detector must recover the carry and stay silent on the null. No network.

| world | excess %/yr | Sharpe | HAC *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| null (`carry = 0`), **12 seeds** | ~0 | mean +0.03 (sd 0.34) | **\|t\| ≥ 2 in 0/12** |
| planted (`carry = 0.012`, seed 888) | +1.77 | +1.73 | **+3.90** (CI [+0.86, +2.58]) |

The detector recovers a planted carry cleanly and never fires on the null — so the real-tape
carry is a genuine effect, not a bug. *(A faithful-engine / power check only — never cited in
support of the real-tape stamp.)*

## Verdict

- **Signal — REAL (thin & regime-bound).** The AAA-CLO carry is a genuine risk-adjusted
  pickup: JAAA earns **+1.38%/yr** over cash on **1.63%** vol — **Sharpe +0.84** (HAC *t* =
  **+2.33**, bootstrap CI [+0.09, +1.72] clear of zero) — the **top** of the excess-vs-excess
  Sharpe race, *above the un-tranched loan collateral it is carved from* (BKLN +0.24), with
  **ICLO independently confirming** (+0.88, *t* = +3.08). Caveats named loudly: the carry lives
  in the high-rate era (ZIRP flat, +0.00%/yr), the CI only just clears zero, and ~5.7y spans a
  single, stress-free credit cycle.
- **Tradability — FRAGILE.** The harvest survives costs and capacity trivially (buy-and-hold
  net **+1.35%/yr**, Sharpe +0.83), but it is thin and its realized Sharpe is flattered by a
  sample with **no CLO stress**: the ~1.4%/yr is the premium for a tail that never fired, so it
  is real-but-fragile, not bankable free money.
